text: Hi, Maria? It's Alex from financial aid at Westbrook State. Daniel's award letter is ready, so I wanted to walk you through it.
Oh, wonderful, thank you. I have it pulled up right here.
Perfect. Okay, big number first. Daniel's total aid package is $31,500.
Oh, thank goodness. So it's covered.

expect.note: Maria reads 'aid package' as free money that covers everything. Alex's next turn corrects it after the private card: $14,000 is loans that must be repaid and $2,500 is work-study.

text: Well, not quite, it isn't all free money. $14,000 of it is loans, which get paid back, and $2,500 is work-study, which Daniel earns at a campus job.
Oh. I'm glad you said that. So how much is actually free?
The grants, $15,000. That's the Westbrook Grant, $9,000, and the federal Pell Grant, $6,000. Grants never get paid back.
Okay. So $15,000 is free, and the rest is loans and his campus job.
That's right. Oh, and Daniel was also selected for verification.
Oh good, so we're verified?

expect.note: Maria thinks 'selected for verification' means already approved. Alex moves on to housing without correcting it, so Beacon asks aloud what it means for her.

text: So, on to housing. Housing and meals are estimated at $16,500 for the year, out of a total yearly cost of $38,000.

Oh, good catch, thank you. Maria, sorry, I went right past that. Verification means the school needs more documents from you, like tax return transcripts and a verification worksheet. They're due July 15, or Daniel's aid could be delayed or canceled.
Oh, I had that backwards. So we still owe paperwork, and it's due July 15.
Exactly. Now, to keep the Westbrook Grant, Daniel needs to maintain SAP each term.
...Okay.

expect.note: Alex says 'SAP' without defining it; Maria hesitates for three seconds and replies passively. Alex explains SAP in his next turn after the private card.

text: Sorry, let me explain. SAP is Satisfactory Academic Progress. Each term, Daniel needs at least a 2.0 GPA, about a C average, and has to complete at least 67 percent of the credits he attempts.
Got it, a C average, and he finishes 67 percent of the credits he attempts. Um, does the work-study money have to be paid back?

expect.note: Alex skips the question for three turns of portal logistics: the private card appears after the second, and Beacon reminds him aloud after the third. Alex then answers: it is earned as paychecks, never repaid, and not credited to the bill upfront.

text: So, next step. You'll accept the awards in the student portal, and you can accept or decline each one separately.
Once you submit, you'll get an email confirmation.
And you can change your mind on any award until the first day of classes.
Oh, you're right, I skipped your question, Maria. No, work-study isn't paid back. Daniel earns the $2,500 as paychecks from a campus job. It just isn't credited to the bill upfront.
Oh, okay. So it's his paycheck, not a loan, but it won't lower the bill upfront.
Right. And he qualified for work-study partly because of your SAI, which came from the FAFSA you filed.
Oh, he'll be thrilled. He's already talking about working at the campus library. He practically lives there.

expect.note: recap at most; must never be spoken

text: Ha, I love that. Tell him to apply early, those jobs go fast.
Beacon, what's a Parent PLUS loan?

expect.note: Maria uses the wake word. Beacon answers aloud from the glossary and letter: borrowed by the parent, optional, separate application and credit check, $8,500 offered.

text: Yep, that's exactly right. And I'd underline the optional part. You don't have to decide on it today.
Okay, good. That's a big one, so I'd like to think it over.
Totally fair. So here's the whole picture. The full cost is $38,000. Accepting every piece of aid, including the Parent PLUS loan, covers $31,500, which leaves $6,500 for your family to pay.
So even taking every loan and the work-study, we'd still need $6,500 of our own.
Right. The letter also lists a net price of $23,000. That's the full cost minus only the grants, the free money.
Okay, $38,000 minus the $15,000 in grants. So $23,000 is what we'd cover with loans, work-study, and our own money.
So, next steps. Accept or decline each award in the student portal, and send the verification documents by July 15.
Got it. Awards in the portal, documents by July 15. Thank you so much, Alex, this really helped.
You're so welcome, Maria. And congratulations to Daniel!
Thank you! Bye now.
